subject: StormPoint performance escalation — executive coordination & customer update
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@stormpoint.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jacob Mills <jmills@cloudops.stormpoint.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: production latency & 5xx spike across inference cluster

Hi Neha —

We started seeing tail latency jump and an uptick in 500s on our production routing to Redwood hosted model redwood/gpt-14x at ~07:50 PT. Error rate peaked at ~9.2% for a 20-minute window and throughput dropped ~38% during that period. Our users in EU and US experienced degraded response times (p95 from ~240ms -> ~1.2s).

This is impacting several customer-facing flows. We've opened PD-48291 on our side and attached sample traces and the earliest error bundle. Can your team confirm whether this is a runtime, autoscaler, or model variant regression? We need an exec-level sync and a shared war-room while we investigate.

Attaching: stormpoint-sample-traces.json (excerpt), error-sample-20260904.log

—Elena

- War-room open (PD link below). Marcus and Rishi are taking lead on runtime/serving.

Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 09:01:00 -07:00
Subject: URGENT: StormPoint war-room — role assignments & immediate actions

Team —

We have a high-severity customer escalation for StormPoint (see Elena's note). PD-48291 is active. Quick assignments:

- Marcus (runtime): Triage kernel selection / recent kernel rollout; check kernel telemetry and rollback health on canary.
- Rishi (model infra): Verify KV cache consistency and model shard health (partial OOMs could explain 500s).
- Dylan (logs/ingest): Pull full error bundle and upload to shared Drive, preserve earliest window (07:40–08:10 PT). Attach to INF-1137.
- Jonas (routing): Check smart routing rules and fallback behavior; confirm whether automatic fallback triggered to a slower quantized variant.
- Lauren (customer/sales): Prepare a short exec-level note for StormPoint leadership and be ready to discuss service credit policy if required.

Keep updates within the war-room thread. If you need extra quota to scale a warm standby, state the amount and I will approve immediately.

We will do status checks at T+30 / T+60 / T+120.

Neha
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: StormPoint war-room — role assignments & immediate actions

Quick technical update — after initial triage:
- Observed: A recent kernel-selector update deployed at 07:35 PT increased aggressive fusion heuristics on longer-sequence workloads. Canary nodes are showing increased memory pressure leading to intermittent 500s when KV swap occurs.
- Action taken: Rolled back kernel-selector to previous stable profile on affected canary pool (rolled to pool-wn-4/wn-5).
- Short-term mitigation: We scaled +30% warm standby capacity for StormPoint routing and disabled the aggressive fusion heuristic in the canary.
- Logs attached: latency-sample-traces.json and stormpoint-error-logs.tar.gz (uploaded to Drive).

Preliminary impact (post-rollback, 09:20 PT): error rate reduced to ~1.4%, throughput recovering to ~92% of baseline, p95 back to ~310ms. Continuing to monitor for regression during sustained traffic.

Next steps: hold rollback until we complete a deeper memory/buffer analysis (Rishi), then prepare a re-release candidate with safer heuristics and a targeted canary. ETA for re-release: 48 hours if no blocker.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: StormPoint — status update (T+~2h) and next steps

Hi Elena / Jacob —

Thanks again for flagging: quick summary of what we've done and the current status.

What happened
- A runtime kernel-selector change at ~07:35 PT introduced an aggressive fusion path for long sequences which increased memory pressure under StormPoint's traffic pattern, causing intermittent 500s and throughput degradation.

What we did
- Rolled back the kernel-selector for the affected canary pools and disabled the heuristic.
- Scaled warm standby by +30% for StormPoint routing to reduce request queuing.
- Collected full traces and error bundles (attached).

Current status (10:00 PT)
- Error rate: ~1.4% (down from 9.2% peak)
- Throughput: ~92% of baseline and trending up
- Latency p95: ~310ms (target baseline ~240ms)

Immediate next steps
- Our SREs (Rishi/Marcus) will perform a memory/buffer root-cause analysis and validate a conservative kernel profile for a safe re-release (target: 48h).
- We'll run an expanded canary for 4 hours before any rolling changes; we will not auto-redeploy without an explicit hold from StormPoint.
- We will schedule an executive readout at 16:00 PT today to review impact, credit policy, and mitigation plan. If that time doesn’t work, propose alternatives.

Attachments: runbook-war-room.pdf (war-room actions), stormpoint-error-logs.tar.gz, latency-sample-traces.json

Please let me know the three customer routes / API keys you want prioritized and I’ll make sure those have pinned capacity during the canary window.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: StormPoint — executive readout & follow-ups (post-mortem next steps)

Folks —

Quick executive summary we will share with leadership tomorrow morning:
- Incident: kernel-selector heuristic caused memory pressure leading to 500s; rollback mitigated user impact.
- Customer impact: short window of elevated errors (peak 9.2%) and a 38% throughput dip; partial recovery following rollback.
- Actions: deep RCA (Marcus/Rishi), re-release with conservative profile (48h ETA), extended canary + customer-pin capacity, final post-mortem and proposed service credit (billing) by EOD Monday.

Requests:
- Marcus/Rishi: provide RCA draft and mitigations list by 09:00 PT Monday.
- Neha: consolidate customer communications and proposed credit language; I will coordinate with Sales/legal.
- Jonas/Dylan: attach routing and logs evidence to INF-1137; preserve all telemetry for 90 days.

Good work today. We contained the blast radius and kept the customer informed in real time — that helped avoid escalation to legal.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
